deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a continuous German prose passage of historical notes on the wars of the Diadochi, the successors of Alexander the Great. The previous and next pages continue the same narrative, so the page probably belongs to lecture or reading notes on ancient history. The hand, a fairly regular Kurrent, may not be Gauss's own.

Content, restated:
- Meanwhile Antipater died (dated 320 in the text).
- Antipater had chosen Polysperchon as his successor and passed over his own son Cassander.
- Discord followed. Cassander went over to Antigonus, and Polysperchon remained in Macedonia.
- Eumenes, besieged at Nora (see the previous page), now pretended to want peace, written here as 'with Polysperchon'. He asked for permission or a parley; this phrase is uncertain.
- Antigonus sent him an oath that he was to swear to the king(s).
- Eumenes swore it, but with a small alteration.
- He then tried to gather his scattered troops again.
- Still not strong enough, he went into upper Asia (Oberasien) to obtain help. The sentence continues on the next page: 'zu bekommen'.

No derivation, computation, or mathematical problem is present, so there is nothing to reconstruct mathematically.
errors: Historical dating: Antipater died in 319 BC; the page gives 320.

Historical slip: according to Plutarch (Eumenes 12) and Diodorus (18.53, 18.58–18.59), the feigned negotiations at Nora were with Antigonus, not Polysperchon. Antigonus sent the oath (via Hieronymus), and Eumenes altered it to include Olympias and the kings. Polysperchon's later offer of command comes on the next page. The phrase 'Friede mit Polysperchon' is therefore probably a slip for Antigonus, unless the writer meant it differently.
No mathematical errors are possible, since the page has no mathematical content.

results.what: Narrative notes on the Diadochi: the death of Antipater, the succession of Polysperchon, Cassander's defection to Antigonus, and Eumenes' altered oath at Nora

transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'zum Nachfolger gewählt' may instead read 'zum Nachfolger ernannt'; the image is ambiguous.

Lines 6–7: 'bat sich {+die+} Erlaubniß[?] gegen[?] aus[?]' is doubtful. The image shows 'die' inserted above the line, followed by a word broken across the line, 'Er-/…dung' or similar. It may read 'Unterredung' (parley), which would fit the history; it remains uncertain.
Line 8: 'einen Eid[?]' — the reading 'Eid' agrees with the image and with the history (the oath sent by Antigonus).
Line 9: 'dem König denen[?] schwören' — the word after 'König' is unclear and might be 'deren' or similar. The meaning is clearly an oath to the king(s).
Line 10: 'Er schwur ihn, aber mit einer kleinen Veränderung' is confirmed.
Last line: 'um Hülfe[?] [?]' — the sentence continues with 'zu bekommen' on the next page, so the reading 'um Hülfe' is plausible and the trailing [?] is probably 'zu' or empty.
